How we got here

School is this way because we chose it.

Assumptions

Made decades ago. Mostly unexamined since.

Choices

Bells. Grades. Seat time. Pacing guides.

The school we have

The one that makes everyone miserable.

None of it is physics.

A menu of traditional assumptions

Nº 01

Learning = letters & numbers

Nº 02

Content over transferable skills

Nº 03

The teacher is the sole expert

Nº 04

Coverage over depth

Nº 05

Age = ability

Nº 06

Time is the constant; mastery is the variable

Nº 07

The bell owns the learning

Nº 08

Compliance before learning

Nº 09

Tests measure schools

Not one of these is a law of nature. Every one is a choice.

And the kids have been telling us.

13%
of 5th–12th graders give school an “A” for making learning exciting
Gallup · Next Gen Insights · 2023
17%
showed grade-level mastery — after meeting the demands of our assignments 71% of the time
TNTP · The Opportunity Myth · 2018
22%
say many or all of their teachers try to understand their lives
YouthTruth · 2022–23
42%
“really feel” like part of their school community
YouthTruth · 2022–23
To put a finer point on it

That last number — 42% belonging — is really three questions:

01

Do students even want to be here?

02

Are the teachers prepared to properly challenge them when they get here?

03

Do both teachers and students feel good about what they accomplish while they’re there?

We picked four. There are… more.

Grades vs. motivation

Grading depressed later achievement for lower-achieving students Klapp, Cliffordson & Gustafsson 2016

Grades measure a blend of achievement + noncognitive factors — noisy gatekeepers Brookhart et al. 2016

Comments-only beats grades for interest & performance Butler 1987 · Butler & Nisan 1986

Grades nudge performance-avoidance; autonomy sustains motivation Pulfrey, Darnon & Butera 2013

Percentage grades distort precision & reliability; avoid 0–100 scales Guskey

Make grades serve learning: clear criteria, recent evidence, re-assessment Brookhart 2017 · Brookhart & Guskey 2019

Motivation & relevance

Meaningful choice boosts motivation and performance Psychological Bulletin 2008 · meta-analysis

Project/problem-based learning raises motivation Educational Psychology Review 2024 · meta-analysis

Relevance drives motivation and achievement Annual Review of Developmental Psychology 2021

Personal-relevance interventions improve outcomes in classroom RCTs JEP: Applied 2018 · PNAS 2023 · Frontiers 2023

AP project-based learning raises odds of AP scores 3+ cluster RCT

Global shift toward creativity and problem-solving OECD PISA 2022 · Vol. III

AI & our kids' futures

Teens expect AI to reshape work — and want prep for it SIAM M3 Challenge 2024

Most teens aren't learning AI in school Junior Achievement 2025

Core skills will shift ~39% by 2030 WEF · Future of Jobs 2025

AI skills are diffusing beyond tech roles Burning Glass Institute 2024

Employers pay wage premiums for AI skills HR Dive 2025

Why we’re talking about AI at all
Before

Time. Bandwidth. Expertise. Coaching. Years of iteration.

Now

It takes the will to change — and a thought partner that never sleeps.

Every assumption on that menu was written in a world where this did not exist.
From the menu · Nº 01

“Evaluating learning means giving grades.”

What it quietly drags along

  • Assessment done to students, not for them
  • Good grades = learning happened

What students keep showing us

  • They volunteer for hard things constantly
  • They’ll tell you what they know — if the telling feels worth it

Wouldn’t it be cool if assessments actually told us what we want to know?

Live demo

Build yourself a thought partner.

The seed prompt

I want assessments that tell me what students actually know — not what they can perform under pressure. Help me rethink how I gather evidence of learning in my subject / grade.

Start by asking me what I really want to know about my students that my current assessments aren’t telling me. Keep everything grounded in modern research, not hype.

Watch what happens

It interviews you first.
It cites research you can check.
Save it as a Gem — on call forever.

Free Gemini, on the district laptop. Everything at bit.ly/prompting-will.

That wasn’t magic. It was four moves.

1

A role and a real constraint

Your subject, your kids, your building.

2

Make it ask you questions first

“Start by asking me…” flips the dynamic.

3

Demand grounding

“Research, not hype” — then go check one.

4

Save it as a Gem

Instructions + your files, saved. That’s the whole tutorial.

From the menu · Nº 03

“The teacher must be the sole expert in the room.”

“I can’t ask my students to create something I don’t know how to create.” Yes, you can.

What this assumption costs

  • Content capped at what one adult knows
  • Whole disciplines vanish when a position goes unfilled

What changes when it vanishes

  • Your real expertise gets promoted: knowing your kids
  • “I don’t know — let’s find out” becomes the lesson plan
Live demo

One big question.

The seed prompt

I teach grade / subject. Take my unit on topic and help me rebuild it around one big question my students would actually argue about at lunch.

Ask me about my kids first. Then help me design 2–3 ways students could show me they’ve learned it — none of which are a worksheet.

And when the expert doesn’t exist…

No art teacher in the building? Arts Integration Coach Gem.
Triage, not replacement — it was Gem vs. zero art.

Both prompts, ready to paste, at bit.ly/prompting-will.
